summary: The device was expected to boot fully with network connectivity. The run completed with 22 events, 0 fatal events, and 0 failures, suggesting a successful boot process at the high level. However, nearly all per-criterion verification evidence (boot_completed, uptime, network IP, dmesg, logcat) consists of 3-byte log stubs with no visible content, leaving three of four criteria unverified. The only concrete evidence — a 16-byte serial boot log — shows a benign SSH host key warning and nothing indicative of crash or panic.
suggested_next: Re-run the boot verification with enhanced log capture: ensure each check step (boot_completed property query, uptime command, ifconfig/ip addr output, dmesg) writes its full stdout/stderr to the evidence log. If the 3-byte logs represent success markers by design, modify the capture mechanism to include the actual command output alongside the marker for auditability.

key_evidence.summary: Run completed with 0 fatal events and 0 failures across 22 total events, indicating no crash or fatal error was detected.
Three verification steps (boot_completed, network-up, dmesg collection) each show only 3-byte logs — no command output was captured to confirm boot property, IP assignment, or dmesg contents.
The serial boot log (16 bytes) contains only an sshd host key warning — no kernel panic, OOM, watchdog reset, boot loop, or ADB timeout was observed.
